summary: Lysidice or Lysidike (Ancient Greek Λυσιδίκη), daughter of Pelops and Hippodamia, married Mestor son of Perseus and became mother of Hippothoe — whose abduction by Poseidon began the Taphian line. Some authors also make her mother of Alcmene by Electryon; Pausanias prefers other stemmata for Amphitryon's house.
etymology: Ancient Greek Λυσιδίκη (Lysidíkē), "releasing justice" or "loose justice."

sections.heading: Wife of Mestor
paragraphs: Apollodorus places Lysidice among Pelops' daughters and makes her consort of Mestor at Mycenae. Their daughter Hippothoe is carried off by Poseidon to the Echinades, where she bears Taphius — ancestor of the Taphian raiders who later kill Electryon's sons.
A rival genealogy sometimes makes Lysidice mother of Alcmene by Electryon; Pausanias explicitly rejects Pelops' daughter Lysidice as mother of Amphitryon, preferring Laonome.

sections.heading: Homonym care
paragraphs: Other Lysidices include a Thespian princess who bore Teles to Heracles, a daughter of Coronus mother of Philaeus by Ajax, and an Aeolid of Lipara. The atlas id lysiddice-pelops is only the Pelopid wife of Mestor.
